The communication maintains a restrictive stance while acknowledging solid real activity, which is consistent with Taylor-rule guidance that prescribes keeping the policy rate above neutral until inflation is clearly converging to target. The insistence on “greater confidence” before easing aligns with New Keynesian Phillips curve frameworks (Calvo pricing; Woodford) in which expectations are central to current inflation dynamics, and with credibility mechanisms designed to mitigate the inflation bias under discretion (Rogoff conservative central banker; Walsh-type contracts). Ongoing balance-sheet runoff (QT) points to slower money growth, a classic disinflationary channel noted in monetarist and DSGE literatures, reinforcing the contractionary impulse from high real policy rates. Although the Committee cites improved risk balance and strong labor markets, the emphasis on inflation risks and commitment to the 2 percent objective keeps the tone cautious rather than dovish. Net effect: mildly positive on growth, restrained by inflation vigilance.
